title: Kings and Queens
intro: Battles, crowns and famous royal moments from a thousand years of British history.

questions.prompt: In which year was the Battle of Hastings fought?
questions.explanation: The Battle of Hastings took place in 1066, when the Normans defeated the English army.

questions.prompt: Who won the Battle of Hastings?
questions.explanation: William, Duke of Normandy, won the battle and became known as William the Conqueror.

questions.prompt: Which king agreed to Magna Carta?
questions.explanation: King John agreed to Magna Carta, which limited the king's power and said he must follow the law.

questions.prompt: In which year was Magna Carta agreed?
questions.explanation: Magna Carta was agreed at Runnymede, near the River Thames, in 1215.

questions.prompt: How many times did King Henry VIII marry?
questions.explanation: Henry VIII had six wives, one of the most famous facts about the Tudors.

questions.prompt: Which Tudor queen was the daughter of Henry VIII and Anne Boleyn?
questions.explanation: Elizabeth I was the daughter of Henry VIII and his second wife, Anne Boleyn.

questions.prompt: In which year did the Great Fire of London begin?
questions.explanation: The Great Fire of London started in September 1666 and burned for several days.

questions.prompt: The Great Fire of London started in a bakery on Pudding Lane.
questions.explanation: The fire began in Thomas Farriner's bakery on Pudding Lane and spread quickly between the wooden houses.

questions.prompt: Which queen gave her name to an era of British history in the 1800s?
questions.explanation: Queen Victoria reigned from 1837 to 1901, and that time is called the Victorian era.

questions.prompt: Alfred the Great was king of which Anglo-Saxon kingdom?
questions.explanation: Alfred ruled Wessex in the south of England in the 800s and is remembered for defending it against Viking armies.

questions.prompt: Which English king died at the Battle of Hastings?
questions.explanation: King Harold II died during the battle in 1066, and William of Normandy went on to become king of England.

questions.prompt: What is the name of the long embroidery that tells the story of the Norman Conquest?
questions.explanation: The Bayeux Tapestry is about 70 metres long and shows the events leading up to and including the Battle of Hastings.

questions.prompt: William the Conqueror ordered a great survey of who owned land in England. What is it called?
questions.explanation: The Domesday Book recorded land, people and animals across much of England, so the king knew what taxes could be paid.

questions.prompt: In which year was the Domesday survey carried out?
questions.explanation: The survey was made in 1086, twenty years after the Norman Conquest.

questions.prompt: Which English king was known as "the Lionheart"?
questions.explanation: Richard I earned the name Lionheart because of his reputation for bravery.

questions.prompt: Richard the Lionheart spent most of his ten-year reign living in England.
questions.explanation: Richard spent only about six months of his reign in England. He was away on crusade or defending his lands in France.

questions.prompt: Which Scottish king won the Battle of Bannockburn in 1314?
questions.explanation: Robert the Bruce defeated the English army of Edward II at Bannockburn, a famous moment in Scottish history.

questions.prompt: Which queen of the Iceni tribe led a rebellion against the Romans in Britain?
questions.explanation: Boudicca led the Iceni and other tribes against Roman rule around AD 60 to 61.

questions.prompt: King Cnut ruled England as well as Denmark.
questions.explanation: Cnut, sometimes spelled Canute, was a Danish king who also ruled England from 1016 until 1035.

questions.prompt: When Elizabeth I died in 1603, which Scottish king also became king of England?
questions.explanation: James VI of Scotland became James I of England, so for the first time one king ruled both kingdoms.

questions.prompt: Who ruled as Lord Protector in the 1650s, when England had no king?
questions.explanation: After the English Civil War, Oliver Cromwell led the country as Lord Protector from 1653 until 1658.

questions.prompt: What is the name for the time in 1660 when Charles II became king and the monarchy returned?
questions.explanation: The Restoration means the return of the monarchy, when Charles II came back to rule after years without a king.

questions.prompt: Queen Anne was the last monarch from the Stuart family.
questions.explanation: Anne died in 1714 without any surviving children, and the crown passed to George I from Hanover.

questions.prompt: Who was Queen Victoria's husband?
questions.explanation: Victoria married Prince Albert in 1840. The Royal Albert Hall in London is named after him.

questions.prompt: Queen Victoria reigned for more than 60 years.
questions.explanation: Victoria reigned for over 63 years, from 1837 to 1901.

questions.prompt: For about how many years was Elizabeth II queen?
questions.explanation: Elizabeth II became queen in 1952 and reigned until 2022, about 70 years, the longest of any British monarch.

questions.prompt: Who was the father of Queen Elizabeth II?
questions.explanation: George VI became king in 1936, and his elder daughter Elizabeth became queen after him in 1952.

questions.prompt: Which royal family name did King George V choose in 1917?
questions.explanation: George V changed the family name to Windsor, after Windsor Castle, during the First World War.

questions.prompt: Where in London are the Crown Jewels kept?
questions.explanation: The Crown Jewels, including crowns worn at coronations, are kept safe and shown to visitors at the Tower of London.

questions.prompt: In which London church have most English and British monarchs been crowned since 1066?
questions.explanation: Coronations have taken place at Westminster Abbey since William the Conqueror was crowned there on Christmas Day 1066.
